transcript:
Meeting Header:
Date: 2027-02-14
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Blake (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Mark Chen (CISO, Valence), Leila Ortiz (Head of Compliance), Tariq Hassan (Cloud Architect), Erin Park (Legal)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be imperfect):
Redwood gives an overview of their compliance artifacts; customer asks for scoping and evidence process, discusses encryption and KMS routing, RBAC and SSO, data residency. Agreement to share redacted reports and set up controls mapping session.

[00:00:05] Jordan Blake: Hey everyone thanks for taking time, uh, we're going to run through our compliance posture and make sure we align on what Valence needs for SOC 2 / ISO. 
[00:00:12] Mark Chen: Thanks Jordan, I got a hard cut at 16:00 but we'll try to cover the essentials, I'm mostly interested in the evidence flow and how you provide read-only access to reports.
[00:00:20] Priya Nair: Great, I'll take most of the technical questions — quick note, apologies if the transcript misnames things, I sometimes say Redwood Dedicate instead of Dedicated, ignore that if you see it.
[00:00:30] Leila Ortiz: Sure — and Erin from legal is on for contract / data residency questions.
[00:00:36] Erin Park: hi all.

[00:02:10] Jordan Blake: Ok, quick slide: we host SOC 2 Type II and ISO27001 summary reports in our trust portal. For customer side we can: provide a redacted PDF of the full SOC2 Type II, grant a read-only trust center user, or set up a short evidence export for auditors.
[00:02:35] Mark Chen: When you say trust portal is that the console or a separate site? we need to know who can see PII.
[00:02:43] Jordan Blake: it's the Redwood Console trust center — one-click access but we can restrict to an enterprise-only view for your org; it's read-only and audit-trailed. We log access events.
[00:03:05] Tariq Hassan: do you push the audit logs somewhere or do we pull them? how's log retention handled?
[00:03:12] Priya Nair: We have an export endpoint and a retention policy — default 90 days for actionable logs but we do offer extended retention as an add-on, and we can ship daily exports to your S3 or to your SIEM via encrypted transfer. There's also an immutable store for compliance retention if needed.

[00:05:20] Leila Ortiz: For our internal auditors we need the actual control mappings — which controls are in scope and who's the owner at Redwood. Can you map your SOC controls to Valence's control framework?
[00:05:30] Jordan Blake: Yeah, that's exactly what the workshop would be for — Priya will run a control-by-control mapping and we'll flag gaps and evidence artifacts. We'll produce a controls matrix that maps SOC/ISO controls to Redwood artifacts and show the owner contact.
[00:05:45] Priya Nair: For example, access control — we map to SOC CC6 and ISO A.9 — owners are our infra security lead; evidence includes SSO logs, RBAC policy exports, and provisioning runbooks.

[00:07:55] Mark Chen: On SSO: we use Okta, SCIM provisioning, and strict group scoping. How does Redwood handle RBAC provisioning and deprovisioning?
[00:08:02] Priya Nair: We support SAML/SSO and SCIM for user provisioning. Most customers do SCIM to automate groups. We also have role templates in the Console that can be tied to Okta groups; deprovision flows are event-driven and we emit provisioning logs to the audit trail.
[00:08:16] Mark Chen: is there a self-service user creation? we need ephemeral tokens for service accounts.
[00:08:21] Jordan Blake: We support short-lived API keys and token rotation; for service accounts you can issue scoped tokens and we advise putting them into your vault. We also support KMS-wrapped keys for extra guardrails.

[00:10:40] Tariq Hassan: KMS — talk me through options. We run in multiple regions (US-East, EU-West) and we use customer-managed KMS keys in AWS and occasionally Azure. Can Redwood integrate with customer KMS/HSM?
[00:10:50] Priya Nair: Yes. We support external KMS where keys are customer-owned — you can bring your own key (BYOK) and we do envelope encryption. For HSMs we have a flow for on-prem HSM connectors; some customers prefer using an HSM in front of the key. We'll share a diagram.
[00:11:10] Mark Chen: Is the key ever exported or is it purely used in place?
[00:11:15] Priya Nair: Keys remain in your KMS; Redwood only receives wrapped keys or encrypted tokens. We never persist plaintext customer master keys.

[00:12:40] Erin Park: legally, we want to see the contract language for key ownership and breach notification windows. Who do we talk to?
[00:12:47] Jordan Blake: I'm the AE but I'll loop in our legal ops; I can pull the standard KMS addendum and send it as part of the package.

[00:14:00] Leila Ortiz: About data residency — we need confirmation that data stays in EU or US regions depending on scope. Can you guarantee region-only processing?
[00:14:08] Priya Nair: Yes, we have region pinning. You can pin workloads to specific regions and we can route inference and storage accordingly; there are some tradeoffs on latency if you restrict to a single region, but it's supported.

[00:15:20] Mark Chen: Audit logs — what fields do you capture? request metadata, IP, user agent, token id?
[00:15:27] Priya Nair: We capture timestamp, request path, model id, token usage, requester id, source IP, region, and whether a fallback was used. We also capture invocation metadata for function/tool calls. The logs are queryable in the Console and exportable.

[00:17:05] Jordan Blake: A common question is how we handle fallback model routing for reliability — that shows up in the logs and in the SLO metrics. If you rely on strict model determinism for compliance we can disable automatic fallbacks per route.
[00:17:23] Tariq Hassan: Good to know. For the controls mapping, do you have a sample matrix?
[00:17:28] Priya Nair: Yes, we have a sample control mapping we send to customers; it maps SOC control IDs to Redwood artifacts, the evidence type (logs, config snapshot, runbook), retention, and the owner. We'll send the template before the workshop.

[00:19:50] Mark Chen: One of our auditors asked about encryption in transit — TLS versions, ciphers, and mutual TLS options for internal comms.
[00:19:58] Priya Nair: TLS 1.2+ with modern ciphers; we support mTLS for certain private endpoints in Dedicated/Private deployments. For our Hosted API, standard TLS termination is used plus strict HSTS.

[00:21:12] Leila Ortiz: How do you surface SOC 2 findings? are there outstanding items or exceptions in your latest report?
[00:21:20] Jordan Blake: We'll share a redacted copy of the most recent Type II — there were two minor operational findings from last cycle that are closed; we'll call them out in the cover note.

[00:22:40] Erin Park: Can you do a short summary of the closed findings? we need language for our legal and auditors.
[00:22:46] Jordan Blake: Sure — it's mostly about a tagging policy enforcement gap that was remedied with an automated job. I'll include the remediation notes in the redacted report.

[00:24:15] Tariq Hassan: For private deployments we have narrow net policies — does Redwood support an air-gapped on-prem package?
[00:24:22] Priya Nair: We do offer an on-prem private deployment package with an air-gapped option; it's more of an enterprise engagement and includes offline installers and a slightly different evidence collection process.

[00:26:30] Mark Chen: Ok, timeline question — if we wanted to onboard for review before our audit in late April, what's feasible?
[00:26:38] Jordan Blake: If we start the controls-mapping workshop within the next week or two and you provision a trust center read-only account, we can produce the control matrix and evidence artifacts within 3 weeks. That fits your late-April audit window.

[00:28:50] Leila Ortiz: Are there any required dependencies from Valence to make the mapping work?
[00:28:56] Priya Nair: We'll need your control matrix or list of scoped controls and a point of contact for each control owner. Tariq's team will need to provide VPC architecture and SCIM/Okta configs for provisioning evidence.

[00:30:10] Mark Chen: Regarding encryption at rest for embeddings and KV cache — I heard something about KV cache earlier, how is that stored?
[00:30:18] Priya Nair: The KV cache is encrypted at rest with your chosen key material when using customer KMS; otherwise Redwood-managed keys are used. For regulated data we recommend customer-managed keys plus strict lifetime settings.

[00:32:00] Jordan Blake: Quick note: sometimes the export names get garbled in the transcript — you might see kay vee cache spelled out.

[00:33:15] Erin Park: For legal we need to see breach notification timelines and data processor agreement text, specifically around subprocessors and data transfers.
[00:33:22] Jordan Blake: Understood — I'll add legal ops to the exchange and send standard DPA and subprocessor list.

[00:35:05] Tariq Hassan: Are there built-in controls for model access rate limiting and throttling that auditors might want to see?
[00:35:12] Priya Nair: Yes, rate limits are per-token and per-route; we keep historic quotas and can show per-route throttling logs as evidence.

[00:36:40] Leila Ortiz: For the workshop, what prep should we do?
[00:36:44] Priya Nair: Provide your control scope (CSV or spreadsheet), listing control IDs, description, and owner. Also share your desired retention windows for logs and any residency constraints. We'll circulate the sample matrix and a calendar invite.

[00:38:20] Jordan Blake: Let's recap the immediate asks: redacted SOC2 upload, trust-center read account, KMS diagram, controls mapping workshop. Anything else?
[00:38:32] Mark Chen: That's it from my side. We'll confirm dates for the workshop.
[00:38:40] Erin Park: I'll follow up on legal questions once I see the DPA and subprocessor list.

[00:40:00] Jordan Blake: Great, we'll send the package by Wednesday. Thanks everyone.
[00:40:08] Priya Nair: Thanks, bye.
[00:40:12] (call ends)

Notes on transcript quality: speaker turns sometimes generic (Speaker 2), and a few technical terms transcribed incorrectly (e.g., "kay vee cache" for KV cache).
